---
title: "18 · Functional clustering, end to end"
execute:
  enabled: false
---

A complete workflow, from raw data to an evaluated clustering. Small spatial
units are grouped into functional clusters by combining three relations between
them: `contig` (spatial contiguity, from `contiguity_graph()` over the
polygons), `15_min_walk` (pedestrian accessibility, from `bridge_nodes()` plus
`add_metapaths_by_weight()` over the street network), and `15_min_multi` (the
same with the GTFS bus network added, excluding the pairs already reachable on
foot). `contig` is the homogeneous reference, two units related if they touch;
the other two carry a far less local hypothesis about what makes two units
alike.

The study area is central São Paulo, and the units are a 250 m grid rather than
census tracts. A grid is a worse unit, respecting neither population nor
morphology, but it plays the same role in the graph mechanics and needs no
separate download. The last section records how to swap in real boundaries, a
different transit feed and Overture place categories.

PyTorch is not installed in Blender's Python, so `gdf_to_pyg()` and anything
that learns an embedding cannot run here. The notebook builds the full
heterogeneous graph with its 23 attributes anyway, then clusters it with
PCA + K-Means and scores the result by silhouette and by modularity per
relation.
